page.layout: One page of text, one column. Running head at the top, centred. Below the text, a signature at the lower left and a catchword at the lower right. One marginal note in the right margin, beside the paragraph "Vetulorum gallorum".

main_text.p: aquilas, coruos, miluios, accipitres ambos, fringillarium & palumbarium, hirundines &c, aues item nocturnas, & falcones.

Atque hic eft præcipuarum magisque confeflarum ac noftris terris familiarium avium catalogus, externas, peregrinas, & nouas perfequi parum ad inftitutum norum attinet. Nunc in vfu menfarum quæ præcipuæ fint, difpiciendum.
main_text.head: De gallis gallinaceis.
main_text.p: Gallinaceos ex Perfide primum in alias terras tranfiffe prodiderunt graeci. Ex his fiunt capi, lautiorum hodie menfas plurimum opulentantes. Caftrantur autem galli tum vt facilius pinguefcant, tum vt fuaui-ores reddantur ac delicatiores. Caftrantur nouiffima parte fua alui eximendo tefticulum, vtrumq;. Quod fi enim alter relinquatur, cu-rietur ac canet, coitumq; repetet. Elegantiores quoq; & maiores euadunt, fi caftrentur dum crefcunt.
Vetulorum gallorum carnes ingrata funt & infuaues, fed jus in quo decoquuntur in aluo foluenda celebratur, juniorum vero gallorum Ius gal-lorum. & gallinarum carnes & jus eximie nutriunt.

page.notes: The right margin note "Ius gal-lorum." is set beside the paragraph on old cocks; its position is approximate. The catchword "quam" is uncertain: it may read "guam" or "quæ" on the scan. The word "menfas" and the spelling "juniorum" are read from a faint scan. The running head is printed with a full stop, transcribed here without it. The signature "Y 3" is uncertain in its first letter.
